# Stack VM runtime strategies (Agent 2)

Retrospective ticket for C-level / boundary-relaxed optimizations on top of
Agent 1 tagged bytecode. Surface language unchanged; LOCAP techniques are
documented in `_stack_c.pyx` module docstring.

## Strategy: inline primitive dispatch

Hot `run_wordbuf` branches call `cdef inline exec_*()` for primitives instead of
`_op_*()` wrappers, reducing per-instruction call and error-path overhead.
Surface handlers (`_op_dup`, etc.) delegate to `exec_*` for `TAG_CALL_FN` paths.

## Strategy: loop-invariant body hoisting

`*_incr_le` resolves `body_id` once to `WordBuf*` or `op_fn_t` before the
million-iteration loop, avoiding `run_quoted_body` branch and id lookup each trip.

## Strategy: nogil fast interpreter (`interpret_gil_free`)

Bodies marked `WordBuf.gil_free` (DFS at compile end) run under `with nogil:` via
unchecked stack ops (`u_push_*` / `u_pop_*`) with no `PyErr_Occurred` per pop.
`TAG_CALL_FN`, `TAG_LIT_STR`, `TAG_IF_NZERO`, `TAG_WHILE_IDS` force slow path.

## Strategy: frameless inner loops

When `gil_free`, `*_incr_le` and `run_while_loop_bufs` call `interpret_gil_free`
directly in inner loops instead of `run_wordbuf` (skips RefNanny + `call_depth`
per iteration). Stack depth is asserted sane on `run_op` re-entry only.

## Strategy: incremental stash

Apply `stash@{0}`: `agent2: stack VM runtime LOCAP peephole` on top of Agent 1
commit. Only `imgcomp/_stack_c.pyx` changes.
